To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the onset of capillarization is a consequence of the interaction between the endothelial cell layer and the extracellular matrix, and that the endothelial cells lining the nascent capillaries are a consequence of the onset of sprouting.
the onset of capillaries in angiogenesis can be modeled as the result of the collapse of the endothelial lamina, and that endothelial cells are present in the nascent capillaries.

a mathematical model for the onset of capillarization, which couples a reinforced random walk model for cell movement with Michaelis-Mentan kinetics for the conversion of angiogenic factor to proteolytic enzyme, predicts that endothelial cells form a layer on the nascent capillaries at the onset of angiogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modeling of capillary formation, which is the initial stage of angiogenesis.
the mathematical modeling of the first stage in the formation of a new capillary.
the mathematical modeling of the onset and growth of capillary angiogenic sprouts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model is consistent with the experimental observations and the biological evidence.
the onset of capillaries in angiogenesis is the result of a reinforced random walk coupled to a Michaelis-Metnishen type mechanism.
this model provides a new approach to the modeling of angiogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model predicts that endothelial cells are attracted to angiogenic agents, aggregate, and collapse their laminae to form a new capillary.
we are able to model a single cell in a tissue matrix, and predict the formation of capillaries in the extracellular matrix.
we have developed the theory of reinforced stochastic processes to model the onset of capillarization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the onset of vascular growth is not a random process, as has been assumed in previous models.
a single layer of cells can form a capillary, without the need for a second layer of cells, and without the need for the cells to migrate.
the endothelial cells are the catalyst for angiogenesis, and not the angiogenic factor.
